title: How long is Britain's coast?
hook: Measure the same coast twice with different rulers. Do you get the same answer?

doesNotKnow: that a measured coastline length depends on the length of the ruler

misconception: Every coast has one true length that careful measuring would find.
objective: The learner can explain that a shorter ruler catches more wiggles and gives a longer coast, so a coastline length only means something with the ruler size stated.

claims.text: On this lesson's outline of Great Britain, a 200 km ruler measures about 2,385 km, 100 km about 2,642 km, 50 km about 3,002 km and 25 km about 3,159 km.
claims.source: Divider walk in Demo.tsx (chords of exactly the ruler length along the largest polygon of the kit's 1:110m 'United Kingdom' shape, on an azimuthal equidistant projection centred on its centroid, scale = 6,371.0088 km per radian), plus the closing part-step. Independent script artifacts/scratch/w1-coast.mjs gives 2,385 / 2,642 / 3,002 / 3,159 km, matching the brief.

claims.text: This outline is coarse: it has 47 corners, so no ruler can measure more than its perimeter, about 3,404 km.
claims.source: The 1:110m Great Britain ring has 48 coordinates (first repeated last), perimeter 3,404 km planar / 3,403 km on the sphere (w1-coast.mjs). A divider total is a sum of chords, so it cannot exceed the polyline's length. Rulers of 10 and 5 km give 3,330 and 3,359 km.

claims.text: A shorter ruler gives a longer coast because it follows bays and headlands that a longer ruler steps across; a coast has no single length, only a length at a stated ruler size.
claims.source: Richardson, L. F. (1961), The problem of contiguity, General Systems Yearbook 6; Mandelbrot, B. (1967), How long is the coast of Britain? Science 156(3775): 636-638.

claims.text: Published lengths for Britain's coast disagree with each other for this reason.
claims.source: Example pair to check: CIA World Factbook, United Kingdom coastline 12,429 km (whole UK); Ordnance Survey figure for Great Britain's coastline, about 17,820 km at mean high water. Builder could not open either (network blocked); the lesson quotes neither number, only that they disagree.

recall.question: Two atlases give very different lengths for the same country's coastline. What is the most likely reason?
options: One of them made an error
They measured with different ruler sizes, or map detail
The coast has moved since one was printed
recall.why: A coastline's measured length grows as the ruler shrinks, so the number depends on how finely it was measured.
